chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabie, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, a man from Hudhayl used to insult the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So that reached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: 'Who is for this one?' So two men from the Ansar stood up and said: 'We are, O Messenger of Allah.' So they went until they came to the Bedouins. So they asked about him, and there he was tending his sheep. So they caught up with him between his family and his sheep. So they did not greet him. So he said: 'Who are you two, and what are your names?' So they said to him: 'Are you so-and-so, son of so-and-so?' So he said: 'Yes.' So they descended and struck his neck.

Muhammad ibn Muslim said: So I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What is your view if a man now were to insult the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), should he be killed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you do not fear for yourself, then kill him.'

key_terms.الْأَنْصَار: The Helpers (Ansar, companions of the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing someone who insults the Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the ruling of *Qatl bi-l-Ghayr* (killing by proxy) for *al-Murtadd al-Mu'tad* or the insulter of the Prophet, illustrating the early precedent where two companions executed a Hudhayli man after verifying his identity. Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the killer is not liable for blood money (*diya*) provided they are confident in their own safety (*la takhaf ala nafsika*), a condition emphasized by Shia jurists to ensure the act is deliberate and secure. This incident serves as a foundational text for the concept of *al-Murtadd al-Mu'tad* being killed without trial in cases of direct insult to the Prophet.
